JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an AI agent pane; read `AGENTS.md` and `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` first. Inside the shell, OrcaSlicer's notifications are held and JusPrin draws them itself: a status pill ("N print issues") in the canvas's lower right, the list it opens, a bubble with Ask AI and Resolve with AI and an "Ignore this warning" link (see "Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications" in `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md`). Check print has its own "Checked, nothing found: … OrcaSlicer warnings" list. On 2026-10-28 a UX walkthrough of the built app (jusprin-newui a684aee37d, Opus 5.5) rated the disagreement high; critique with screenshots at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (frames 1A-05, 1A-07, 1B-05, 2A-01, 2A-03, 2B-03). Kenneth wants to choose between fix options before code is written: first deliverable is an untracked options note in the worktree root, then stop. Rules: page-first for logic that does not touch Orca state; temp docs untracked; fork-stewardship doc before touching OrcaSlicer-owned files; do not commit unless asked. Reproduce: scratch copies of the built .app and of `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` (set `local_machines` to `{}` in the copied conf), launch with `--datadir <scratch>`, open `~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` or `~/Downloads/general_purpose_hook.STL`, let the agent slice.

Problem: the three surfaces that report slice warnings disagree, and the chip never clears. After the cable holder sliced, the agent wrote "there's nothing to fix" and explained the one warning as inapplicable to an open A1 mini, while the canvas showed "1 print issue" with an orange dot; after the hook sliced, the agent said "two warnings, neither needs action" and the chip said 3; Check print said "Checked, nothing found: … OrcaSlicer warnings" with the chip still lit beneath it. The chip's popup shows OrcaSlicer's own text ("open the front door and/or remove the upper glass", advice for an enclosed printer) with Ask AI and Resolve with AI buttons that do not say how they differ. After Ask AI and "Print as is", the chip still said "1 print issue". A person reads a number badge as unresolved problems. Frames 1A-05, 1A-07, 1B-05, 2A-01 and 2A-03 of the critique show each state.

Reproduce in the real app (recipe in the background notes) and map the three sources: the print-issue monitor's `slice_warnings_of` feeding the chip, `slice_report` and the `print-issues` skill feeding the agent, and Check print's checked-list. Explain each count difference you saw (why 3 against two, why bed temperature is in one list and not another). Find what "Ignore this warning" does to the chip and whether the agent can set the same state.
2. Write an untracked options note (`issue-chip-options.md` in the worktree root) with two to four options, each with what the person sees across chip, chat and Check print, where it lives, and a recommendation. Candidates: one shared list of warnings with an ignored flag that the agent's report, the chip and Check print all read, so the agent saying "ignore" marks it ignored and the chip shows "1 ignored" or nothing; a chip that counts only warnings the agent has not addressed; making Ask AI and Resolve with AI one button, or labelling what Resolve changes; showing JusPrin's own wording for OrcaSlicer warnings that assume an enclosed printer when the selected printer is open. Say which parts are page-only and which need the host.
3. Stop and wait for Kenneth to choose. Do not implement before he answers.

Done, after his choice, means: after a slice, the chip, the agent's report and Check print show the same warnings and the same count; a warning the agent dismissed is visibly dismissed on the chip; tests cover the count rule; verified in the real app with screenshots of all three surfaces.

158:### Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications
159-
160-Inside the shell OrcaSlicer's own notifications are held but not drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds: print problems as a status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about, with **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI**; the outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused) as a short confirmation above the pill; and work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export) as an entry in the chat.
161-
162-**OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth.** A notification carries a kind, a level and words. It does not carry the object it is about, so where OrcaSlicer lets its check be asked again, that check is asked once more for the object only.
163-
164-| Piece | Owns |
165-|---|---|
166-| `PrintIssues/NoticeKinds` | Where each of OrcaSlicer's notification kinds goes: the issue list, a confirmation, running work, application state, or nowhere. Every kind is named; a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in this file until someone routes it. |
167-| `PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` | Reads the list on the notification manager's own turn, compares it with what it saw last, and rebuilds only on a change. Asks OrcaSlicer's checks for the object behind a validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an object out of a nozzle's reach and a slicing step warning. Holds no rule about what a problem is. |
168-| `issues_from` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue` | The rule, as plain data with its own tests: an object lookup's entry exists only while OrcaSlicer holds a notification of its kind; a print-problem notification no lookup answers for is a plate-wide issue in OrcaSlicer's words. |
169-| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout`, `IssueOverlay` | Where the pieces go, how they are drawn and how they close, with ImGui inside the canvas's frame through the same overlay hook as the tool strip. The bubble never covers its object, the pill, a confirmation or the tool strip. |
170-| `PrintIssues/WorkFeed` | Work as it starts, moves on and ends. A slice is followed through OrcaSlicer's own events, which carry a percentage and an outcome. Other work is read from the "still running" notifications, which carry neither. |
171-| `AgentHost::begin_work`, `update_work`, `finish_work`; `WorkCard` in the page | The entry in the chat: saved with the project at the place in the timeline where the work started, so a later message reads below it; a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel while it runs; completed in place. The chat panel opens when work starts. Repeats are folded by the page, never in what is saved, and an entry still "running" in a project that was closed mid-run reads as interrupted. |
172-| `PrintIssues/IssueContext`, `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` | The chat message a button sends, and the one way a message enters the chat from outside the page. |
173-
174-Two things are read whether or not a notification exists, because OrcaSlicer's notifications do not cover them in time:
175-
176-- **The slice result.** A path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach, and a filament that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when OrcaSlicer's preview loads the slice, which here means opening Check print. OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the moment the slice ends.
177-- **Why a slice failed.** A critical failure is shown in a dialog and leaves no notification, and no notification says which object the failure named. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is the only place both exist.
178-
179-Rules that follow:
180-
181-- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
182-- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
183-- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
184-- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
185-- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **The two buttons differ only in the sentence**: Ask AI and Resolve with AI send the same context and the turn gets the same tools.
186-- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.
187-- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** or **Resolve with AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.
188-- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.
189-
190-Known limits: application and account notifications (update available, plug-in missing, preset sync conflict) are routed to `App` and drawn nowhere yet. A confirmation shows OrcaSlicer's words and a close button; the actions OrcaSlicer attached to its own notification (open folder, eject, cancel an upload) are not offered. Only a slice has a percentage and a known ending; other work shows a bar with no amount and is recorded as done unless its Cancel was pressed. Uploads and downloads have not been run. The tips and the object size card are not shown.
191-
192-### Agent WebView
193-
194-The production Agent interface is a separate React/TypeScript package that runs locally inside a `wxWebView`. It needs:
195-
196-- a versioned schema for commands and events;
197-- scripted mock conversations that play back the same way every time, for UI tests;
198-- messages that render as they stream in, with a scroll position that does not jump;
199-- written rules for keyboard, focus, shortcuts, clipboard, text selection, and IME (the input method used to type languages such as Chinese and Japanese);
200-- a defined state for each of these: reloading, starting up, an error in the bridge between the page and the app, and the agent being unavailable;
201-- no project state of its own. OrcaSlicer's project state stays in C++.
202-
203-#### Where logic goes: the page first
204-
205-When the same logic could live either in C++ or in a React page, put it in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++. The page is quicker to change: Vite hot-reloads it, while a C++ change means relinking a multi-gigabyte GUI library. The page's tests run in milliseconds under Vitest. The text people read is already written in the page. The text the model reads belongs there too.
206-
207-Strong reasons for C++:
208-
209-- **It reads or changes OrcaSlicer state:** presets, the model, plates, slicing, the device list. The page never owns project state (see the constraints below).
210-- **The app has to guarantee it.** This covers what a tool accepts and refuses, which tools a session may call, and what is sent to the model provider (API keys, access codes, project data). Page code can describe a limit, but only the app can enforce one.
211-- **It has to work without a page:** the MCP server, background work, tests that run without a browser.
212-- **It needs a thread the page does not have, or has to stay alive at times when the page is not.**
213-
214-The printer panel shows how this works. The app sends the page only facts: sizes, spools, which printer a card shows, and what a change altered. The page turns those facts into all of the text:
215-
216-- The page writes the model's instructions in `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` and sends them to the app with `printer_instructions`.
217-- The page writes the panel's own text in `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts`. That is the opening line and the note that goes with each tap. The opening line is sent with `printer_opening`. The note for a tap is sent inside that tap's payload.

description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata:

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

This is a wire smoke client, not a substitute for the Phase 4 Inspector/production-client

import argparse
from contextlib import closing
import http.client
import json
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2026-07-28"


def call(endpoint, method, params=None):
    params = dict(params or {})
    params["_meta"] = {
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": {"name": "jusprin-smoke", "version": "1"},
        "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {},
        "progressToken": "smoke-progress",
    }
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream",
        "MCP-Protocol-Version": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "Mcp-Method": method,
    }
    if "name" in params:
        headers["Mcp-Name"] = params["name"]
    with closing(http.client.HTTPConnection(endpoint.hostname, endpoint.port, timeout=310)) as connection:
        connection.request("POST", endpoint.path, json.dumps({
            "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": "smoke", "method": method, "params": params,
        }), headers)
        response = connection.getresponse()
        if response.getheader("Content-Type", "").startswith("text/event-stream"):
            for line in response:
                if line.startswith(b"data: "):
                    message = json.loads(line[6:])
                    if "result" in message or "error" in message:
                        return message
                    print("Progress:", message.get("params", {}).get("message", ""))
            raise RuntimeError("MCP stream closed without a terminal response")
        return json.loads(response.read())


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("url", help="URL shown by the native MCP connection button")
    parser.add_argument("--changes", help='JSON process patch, e.g. {"wall_loops":4}; applied immediately by JusPrin')

# Print-issue chip, agent report and Check print disagree — options

Untracked working note, 2026-10-28. Branch `claude/issue-chip-options` (cut from `jusprin-newui` a684aee37d, no changes). Waiting on Kenneth's choice; no code written.

## The problem, measured

After a slice, three places report OrcaSlicer's warnings and they give different numbers:

| Case (built app a684aee37d, A1 mini, Bambu PLA Basic) | Chip | Agent | Check print |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cable holder `Tape_4_3MF.3mf`, as opened | **1** (bed temperature) | told about 1, `slice_report` lists 0 → "nothing to fix" | "Checked, nothing found: … OrcaSlicer warnings" |
| Hook STL, on its side, no supports | **2** (bed temperature, floating cantilever) | `slice_report` lists 1 | 1 row |
| Hook STL, on its side, supports on, brim, 4 walls (the walkthrough's state, frame 1B-05) | **3** | "two warnings, neither needs action" | 1 row (timelapse) |

I reproduced all three in a scratch copy of the built app. I sliced and read the lists through the app's own MCP tools (`slice_start`, `workspace_inspect`, `slice_report`), with no model calls. Screen control of the copy was declined, so I have no new screenshots; frames 1A-05, 1A-07, 1B-05 and 2A-01 of the 2026-10-28 critique show these states on screen.

## Why the counts differ

There are two lists, built from the same slice by different rules.

1. **The chip's list** (`PrintIssueMonitor::read_result` and `find_steps`, filtered by `slice_warnings_of` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp`). It takes every warning stored in the slice result that has words, plus the step warnings. The agent gets this list only as a summary on the plate: `sliceWarnings` holds the count, the first message and the number ignored, but no ids and no full list.
2. **`slice_report`'s findings** (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::slice_report`). These are the step warnings plus the slice-result warnings, minus two codes. Check print draws exactly this list (`build_check_print_report`), and the agent reads it for the full list.

The two codes `slice_report` drops are the ones the chip counts:

- **Bed temperature (1000C001).** OrcaSlicer raises it whenever the bed is at or above the filament's softening temperature. It never checks whether the printer has an enclosure. Every PLA profile has a softening point of 45 °C and plate temperatures of 55–65 °C, so this warning fires on **every PLA print**. OrcaSlicer's own window never shows it. Its send dialog skips it, and nothing on its canvas reads these result warnings. The chip is the only place in the app that shows it. `slice_report` follows OrcaSlicer's send dialog and leaves it out.
- **The traditional-timelapse copy (1000C003).** On an open-frame printer (`printer_structure` i3) with traditional timelapse, OrcaSlicer stores the same warning twice: 10018003, then 1000C003 "for older A-series firmware". Both copies have the same words. The chip counts both copies and `slice_report` keeps one. That is why the chip said 3 (bed temperature + timelapse + its copy) while the agent said two: it combined the summary's first message (bed temperature) with `slice_report`'s one finding (timelapse).

Check print also merges rows with the same words for the same object. The chip does not.

**"Ignore this warning"** (`PrintIssueMonitor::set_ignored`) adds the issue's id to a set kept per plate in memory. The pill then stops counting it and reads "1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left. The mark is not saved with the project, and it is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops reporting the warning. **The agent cannot set this mark:** no tool or bridge message reaches it, and neither of the agent's lists carries the ids it would need. `slice_report` and Check print do not know about ignores at all.

**Ask AI and Resolve with AI** send the same context and give the turn the same tools. The only difference is the sentence: "Explain this issue and my options." or "Help fix this issue." The architecture doc states this on purpose ("The two buttons differ only in the sentence").

**No printer setting says whether a printer is enclosed.** The P1P (open) and P1S (enclosed) profiles carry the same keys. Wording that depends on the enclosure needs a list of printer models that JusPrin owns.

Every option below changes only fork-owned files (`PrintIssues/`, `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`, `Shell/CheckPrintReport*`, `Agent/`, the skill). None touches OrcaSlicer's own files.

## Options

### Option 1 — One list, one count rule, read by all three (recommended as the base)

The chip's list becomes the only list. `slice_report`'s findings and Check print's OrcaSlicer section read it through the reader that already feeds `sliceWarnings`. They stop reading the slice result themselves. One rule, kept with `issues_from`/`mark_ignored` and tested there, decides two things:

- **Which warnings exist.** Copies with the same words for the same target are merged into one, which removes 1000C003 everywhere. The bed-temperature warning is decided once for all three (sub-choice below).
- **What counts.** The count is the warnings not ignored. The chip number, `sliceWarnings.count` and Check print's section all use it. Each finding carries its id and `ignored`.

The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
  type: project

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.
